name: c
notes: Root language of the software domain: the preprocessor-free ILP32 integer-C fragment SV-COMP's ReachSafety loop/bitvector tasks are written in — all integer widths through long long, one- and two-dimensional static arrays, goto, non-recursive helper functions (inlined), __VERIFIER_nondet_* as frame-addressed inputs, reach_error via __assert_fail as the bad observable; no pointers, floats, heap, structs, or recursion. Semantics is total and deterministic, chosen to be exactly mirrorable by a bit-vector transition system: two's-complement wrap everywhere, SMT-LIB division-by-zero rules (matching btor2), saturating out-of-range shifts, out-of-range array reads 0 / writes dropped. Execution is a machine over an elaborated CFG — each asgn/havoc/br node is one frame, exactly btor2's stimulus discipline ({"steps": [...]}, s_0 checked first, absorbing HALT/ERR) — so the c--btor2 pair keeps bad AND depth exactly. Validated beyond the vectors by differential testing against clang -O0 -fwrapv on the in-fragment SV-COMP corpus (random recorded-tape stimuli; see runs provenance) — 594 of the 598 in-fragment tasks interpret cleanly, the other 4 are dynamic VLAs refused loudly. Graded stipulated until corroborated by benchmark labels (the domain's anchors). Era-6 revision 1 = the Era-5 c text re-cut and re-admitted; the differential runs against clang are oracle testimony recorded as domain anchors (KERNEL.md §6). Revision 3 replaced the `induction` judge by one built by the RISC-V road, independent of the C-to-BTOR2 encoding. Revision 4 runs that judge over the bounded checker's array engine and gives every C array a btor2 array state of its own, reached only through the one address shape the generator emits for an element under a path condition carrying its bounds guard (scalars stay registerized, so no symbolic address can alias them); certificates about C programs with arrays now discharge where the question lives. Every earlier vector byte-identical; two array programs join the vectors. Revision 5 adds a second certificate form, `ranges`: an interval invariant {"kind": "range-invariant", "nodes": {pc: {slot: [lo, hi]}}} over the very machine the `induction` judge builds (pc over C nodes, HALT = L, ERR = L + 1, scalars registerized, arrays as array states, never constrained), judged by three one-step queries on the same bit-blaster — init, consecution per listed pc, safety — with a constant budget and no search; a payload listing ERR, an array or unknown slot, or a bound outside the slot's type is refused, and so is any range too tight for the initial state, any range that is not inductive, and any reachable node left unlisted. It is the form the C-side abstract interpreters write and the form a btor2--c carry-back targets. interp.py, the vectors, the controls and the induction judge are byte-identical to revision 4.
